children: Young adult apparel retailer Abercrombie & Fitch
will be announcing earnings results this Tuesday before the bell. Here’s what to look for.

Abercrombie and Fitch beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $1.27 billion, up 4.8% year on year. It was a very strong quarter for the company, with EPS guidance for next quarter exceeding analysts’ expectations and a beat of analysts’ EPS estimates.
Is Abercrombie and Fitch a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Abercrombie and Fitch’s revenue to grow 6% year on year, in line with the 6.8% increase it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Abercrombie and Fitch rarely misses Wall Street’s revenue estimates.

Looking at Abercrombie and Fitch’s peers in the apparel and footwear retail segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Gap delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 1.8%, meeting analysts’ expectations, and Boot Barn reported revenues up 15.1%, in line with consensus estimates. Gap traded up 9.7% following the results while Boot Barn was also up 15.2%.

Investors in the apparel and footwear retail segment have had steady hands going into earnings, with share prices flat over the last month. Abercrombie and Fitch is down 15.3% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $170.64 (compared to the current share price of $139.46).
